result.text:
Done — all 29 tests pass unchanged, and the ifs and duplicated code are gone.

## What I did

**Two new polymorphic hierarchies** replace the type checks, both in `CustomerImporter-Recu-1er-Parcial`:

`Identification` (abstract) ← `DNI`, `CUIT`
`ZipCode` (abstract) ← `OldZipCode`, `NewZipCode`

Each hierarchy has the same shape:

- The abstract class finds its subclass instead of branching:
  `Identification class>>typeFor:` detects the subclass whose `type` is `'D'`/`'C'`; `ZipCode class>>typeFor:` detects the one that `canRepresent:` the string (first character a digit or a letter). Neither finding one signals the invalid-type error. This is the same `self subclasses detect:` idiom `Environment class>>current` already used.
- A single instance creation funnel (`numbered:` / `coded:`) validates before creating, so an invalid `DNI`, `CUIT` or zip code cannot exist; the importer just asks `Identification for: record fourth number: record fifth` and `ZipCode for: record fifth`.
- Validation is one `assertIsValidNumber:`/`assertIsValidCode:` in the abstract class that signals the subclass's error message, and one `isValidNumber:`/`isValidCode:` per subclass composed of named predicates (`hasSeparatorsInPlace:`, `hasValidPrefix:`, `hasNumericBody:`…) — the five repeated `self error: 'Invalid CUIT number'` are now one.
- The error texts are class-side messages, and the magic numbers are named (`smallestNumber`, `validPrefixes`, `provinceLettersSize`…).

**Duplication removed across the hierarchies:** `NewZipCode class>>hasValidPartsIn:` reuses `OldZipCode isValidCode:` on the four digits it embeds (a CPA *is* a province letter + an old zip code + three distribution letters), and the repeated `allSatisfy: [:c | c isDigit]` became `String>>hasOnlyDigits`/`hasOnlyLetters`, extensions of the package since they are general-purpose helpers on their parameter's class.

**`Customer` and `Address`** now hold an `identification` and a `ZipCode` object, are created complete (`Customer named:lastNamed:identifiedBy:`, `Address streetNamed:number:town:zipCode:province:`) and have no setters. Their tell-apart protocol just delegates: `hasDNIAsIdentification ^identification isDNI`, `oldZipCodeIfNone: ^zipCode oldCodeIfNone:`, etc., with the default answer in the abstract class and the override in the one subclass that has the value.

`importCustomer` and `importAddress` are now three and two statements with no conditionals.

## Notes

- `ZipCode class>>invalidTypeErrorDescription` answers `'Invalid identification type'` — the copy-paste wording of the original importer, which `test29ZipCodeMustBeOldOrNew` asserts. I kept it (with a one-line comment) because the tests had to stay as they are; it is the one thing I would change if the test could change too.
- I left `importRecord`'s two `ifTrue:` and `assertCustomerWasImported`'s `ifNil:` alone: they come from the original exercise, not from the added type handling.
- `ImportTest` moved to `CustomerImporter-Recu-1er-Parcial-Tests` (class category only; no test method touched).
- Everything lives in the running image; the `CustomerImporter` package has no file name set, so I did not write it out, and I did not save the image — tell me if you want either.
